description: We are OrbitalEdge, building a next-level Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer game! 🚀 Our project combines real-world space physics, rocket manufacturing, crew training, and resource management (fuel, oxygen, and hydrogen) to make learning space science fun and interactive. We are looking for creative coders, designers, and space enthusiasts to join our team and build an amazing educational space experience together!
summary: OUTPOST 100 is an interactive learning game where players build and manage a Moon or Mars base. Players choose their base location, manage critical resources like power, water, food and oxygen, meet ROBO the AI assistant, complete daily missions, and test their knowledge through science challenges. The game uses real NASA concepts about space weather, life support systems and engineering trade-offs to teach young learners what it really takes to live beyond Earth. Players learn by making decisions, solving problems and surviving space hazards in a fun, hands-on mission trainer.
details: OUTPOST 100 – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer OUTPOST 100 is an interactive educational space exploration and survival simulation designed to help students understand the challenges of establishing a sustainable human outpost on the Moon or Mars. The game allows players to choose between a lunar and Martian mission, design their own outpost, manage essential resources, and make critical survival decisions. Players must balance power, food, oxygen, water, and radiation protection while facing simulated environmental hazards and unexpected mission events. They can construct solar panels, greenhouses, habitats, shields, water systems, and rovers using an interactive base-building map. The experience also includes an AI-style robotic assistant called ROBO, educational danger guides, mission objectives, resource management challenges, and space science learning activities. Our main goal is to make space science more engaging and accessible for young learners. Instead of only reading about space exploration, students can experience simplified mission decisions and understand how engineering, scientific thinking, and resource management affect astronaut survival. The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with NASA public APIs used for selected astronomy and Earth-observation information. The application also references Three.js as part of its development environment. What makes OUTPOST 100 creative is its combination of interactive gameplay, educational explanations, base design, and survival-based decision-making in one mobile-friendly experience. Our vision is to inspire the next generation of explorers, scientists, and engineers by helping them imagine what it takes to live beyond Earth. OUTPOST 100 – Your Mission. Your Decisions. Your Future.
